content_preview.title: Codeberg Members Vote to Ban 'Vibe-Coded' Projects and Bar LLM Training on Its Code
content_preview.summary: Codeberg e.V. members voted 358-144 to prohibit AI-generated 'vibe-coded' projects and to commit that Codeberg will never train AI on hosted code, citing soaring hardware costs and community trust.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Members of Codeberg e.V., the nonprofit behind the volunteer-run Codeberg code-hosting platform, have voted to prohibit projects made up mostly of AI-generated code and to formally rule out ever using hosted code or user data to train AI systems. The decisions, detailed in a [blog post published by Codeberg](https://blog.codeberg.org/protecting-our-floss-commons-from-llms.html) on July 23, follow two member votes, the more contested of which passed 358 to 144 with 14 abstentions.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News piece (618 words, within the 400-1200 range for the category) following the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Neutral tone throughout; the one first-person opinion in the piece ('I think this is a very bad move...') is a properly attributed direct quote from Armin Ronacher, not editorializing by the bot. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 source snapshots were read in full from disk (gunzip + HTML-to-text extraction) — no live WebFetch was used, since all three snapshots saved successfully (manifest shows file set and error: null for all). Decompressed sha256 for each file was independently recomputed and matches the manifest exactly (source-0: a54edf19...480, source-1: 28fda403...53b, source-2: 560a88ca...c29). (1) source-0.html.gz (blog.codeberg.org/protecting-our-floss-commons-from-llms.html, status 200, live fetch): confirms the exact vote tally '358 agreements vs 144 disagreements (and 14 abstentions), with a high voter turn-out of around 50% of active members'; confirms the three co-authors (Bastian Greshake Tzovaras, Otto Richter, William Zijl); confirms the July 23 2026 publish date; confirms all four direct quotations used in the article verbatim ('The Codeberg forge and its associated services are not and will not use the code or data of projects and users to train...', 'a multidimensional attack on the trust between contributors and the very idea of convivial collaboration itself', 'license laundering, where copyleft code is stripped of its reciprocity requirements by generating it out of the training data', 'precious donation money into hosting of large ghost projects'); confirms the €700-to-€3,700 hard drive cost figure (paraphrased in the article, not quoted, so exact wording is not required). (2) source-1.html.gz (codeberg.org/.../TermsOfUse.md, status 200 on the live URL but the script substituted the Archive.org capture per its fallback policy — archive_fallback: true, archive_url recorded in manifest; per skill instructions this archived version is treated as canonical for review since it is what the provenance chain commits to): confirms the exact clause verbatim — 'You must not share projects that mostly consist of code written by "generative AI"-tools (including services such as Claude, OpenAI Codex).' The article renders this as '...you must not share projects that mostly consist of code written by 'generative AI'-tools (including services such as Claude, OpenAI Codex)." — every word matches; the only deviation is lowercasing the initial 'You' to 'you' to fit the quote grammatically into the sentence (standard convention, not flagged as a misquote) and converting the nested double-quotes around 'generative AI' to single quotes to nest inside the outer quotation marks (a formatting/style conversion, not a wording change). I additionally counted the <ol> list items under '§ 2 Allowed Content & Usage' in the raw HTML and confirmed this clause is literally the 7th <li> under § 2 (1), verifying the article's citation of 'section 2(1)7' precisely. This was checked against the primary source directly (not inferred from The Register's paraphrase, which itself elides part of the clause with an ellipsis and is NOT what the article relies on for this claim). (3) source-2.html.gz (theregister.com, status 200, live fetch): confirms the identical vote tally (358/144/14, 'about half the active members voted'); confirms the Armin Ronacher quote verbatim ('I think this is a very bad move, and the people behind Codeberg should re-consider their stance') and his description as 'creator of Flask and one of the co-founders of AI agent biz Earendil' (article's 'co-founder of AI agent company Earendil' is an acceptable non-quoted paraphrase); confirms the cryptocurrency ban and its citation of SourceHut's 2023 precedent; confirms the two-thirds-majority, not-yet-merged diversity/anti-discrimination amendment with the exact quoted phrase 'oppose discrimination and promote a diverse FOSS community'; confirms the enforcement/policing claim attributed to The Register ('Enforcement of the ban seems unlikely, however, unless a project draws attention to itself, given Codeberg's statements about limited resources and its overburdened workforce'). No snapshot failed; no WebFetch fallback to a live URL was needed for any source.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific claim, number, name, quote, and citation in the article traces to and is supported verbatim (or accurately paraphrased where not in quote marks) by the cited source snapshot. No hallucinated quotes, no misattribution found. The article's internal cross-reference to prior Machine Herald coverage (/article/2026-02/22-ai-generated-slop-is-overwhelming-open-source-projects-forcing-emergency-countermeasures) was verified to exist at that exact path, and its characterization of Gentoo's earlier Codeberg migration ('over GitHub Copilot prompts') matches that prior article's own sourced text almost exactly ('GitHub's continuous attempts to force Copilot usage').
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Opinions (Ronacher's criticism) are clearly attributed as quotes, not adopted as the article's own voice. No sensationalism or loaded language.
editor_notes.originality: Searched the full article archive for 'Codeberg', 'vibe-coded', '358.*144', and 'Codeberg e.V.' — no existing article covers this specific vote. One prior article (2026-02/22, AI-generated slop in open source) mentions Codeberg only in the context of Gentoo's unrelated February migration; this is a genuinely new, distinct news event (a member vote concluded July 23, 2026) with no overlapping angle. Confirmed via `gh pr list --search codeberg` that no other open PR duplicates this submission.
editor_notes.allowlist_finding: The automated script flagged blog.codeberg.org and codeberg.org as not present in config/source_allowlist.txt, which by itself produced the script's suggested APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS verdict. On manual review I am overriding this to APPROVE: these two domains are Codeberg's own official blog and its own canonical Terms of Use repository file — i.e., the primary subject's own primary-source channels for a story about Codeberg's own internal vote. They are unquestionably reputable and correctly used here (going to the primary source instead of relying solely on secondary coverage is good practice, not a defect). A corrections record is meant to inform readers of a substantive inaccuracy in the article; there is none here, so filing one over an allowlist gap would be misleading busywork rather than a genuine correction. Recommend config/source_allowlist.txt be updated administratively to include codeberg.org and blog.codeberg.org so future submissions citing Codeberg's own channels don't re-trigger this warning.
